ASDC.description: AXL+ SIGLEC6+ dendritic cells (ASDC), a distinct DC subset with both myeloid and plasmacytoid features, expressing high levels of AXL, SIGLEC6, and CD1c.

cDC2.description: Conventional dendritic cell type 2 (cDC2) expressing CD1c, FCER1A, and CLEC10A, involved in antigen presentation and T-cell activation.

pDC.description: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDC) specialized in type I interferon production, expressing CLEC4C (CD303), LILRA4, and TCF4.

CD14+ Monocytes.description: CD14+ classical monocytes expressing high levels of CD14, CD16, and CSF1R, with roles in phagocytosis and inflammation.

B intermediate.description: An intermediate B cell population representing a transitional state between naive and memory B cells, expressing high levels of CD24, CD38, and CD21.

B naive.description: Naive B cells that have not yet encountered antigen, characterized by high expression of IgD and IgM, and lacking CD27.

B memory.description: Memory B cells that have undergone class switching and affinity maturation, expressing CD27 and CD38, and lacking surface IgD.

Classical monocyte.description: Classical monocytes are phagocytic cells that circulate in blood, expressing high levels of CD14 and CD16, and are part of the innate immune system.

Switched memory B cells.description: Memory B cells that have undergone class-switch recombination, expressing IgG, IgA, or IgE, and are CD27+ IgD-.

Unswitched memory B cells.description: Memory B cells that retain IgM and IgD, typically CD27+ IgD+, and are involved in T-independent responses.

Atypical memory B cells.description: CD11c+ T-bet+ memory B cells often expanded in autoimmune diseases and infections, with low CD21 expression.

Naive B cells.description: Mature B cells that have not yet encountered antigen, expressing IgM and IgD, with high CD21 and CD23.

Plasmablasts.description: Short-lived antibody-secreting cells derived from activated B cells, characterized by high CD38 and CD138, and low CD20.

B naive.description: Naive B cells expressing surface IgM and IgD, with high levels of CD20 and naive markers.

B memory.description: Memory B cells expressing CD27 and class-switched immunoglobulins, providing anamnestic responses.

Plasma cell.description: Terminally differentiated B cells secreting antibodies, characterized by high CD38 and expression of XBP1.

CD4+ naive T.description: Naive helper T cells expressing CD4, CD62L, and CCR7, responsible for adaptive immune responses.

CD8+ naive T.description: Naive cytotoxic T cells expressing CD8, CD62L, and CCR7, capable of differentiating into effector cells.

Classical monocytes.description: Classical CD14++ monocytes are highly phagocytic and express high levels of CD14 and pro-inflammatory cytokines, serving as the predominant monocyte subset in peripheral blood.

Intermediate monocytes.description: Intermediate CD14++CD16+ monocytes exhibit a pro-inflammatory profile with high antigen presentation capacity and are expanded in inflammatory conditions.

Non-classical monocytes.description: Non-classical CD14+CD16++ monocytes patrol the vasculature, express low levels of CD14, and are involved in wound healing and antiviral responses.

Myeloid dendritic cells (cDC2 - CD1c+).description: CD1c+ myeloid dendritic cells are potent antigen-presenting cells that express CD1c and FCER1A, and are specialized in activating CD4+ T cells.

Plasmacytoid dendritic cells.description: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells are specialized in type I interferon production in response to viral infections and express high levels of IL3RA and CLEC4C.

CD16+ Monocyte (Non-classical).description: Non-classical monocytes expressing high levels of FCGR3A (CD16) and low levels of CD14, involved in patrolling and pro-inflammatory responses.

CD14+ Monocyte (Classical).description: Classical monocytes expressing high levels of CD14, with strong phagocytic and antimicrobial functions.

Intermediate Monocyte (CD14+CD16+).description: Intermediate monocytes co-expressing CD14 and CD16, bridging classical and non-classical monocytes with roles in inflammation and antigen presentation.

Natural Killer (NK) Cell.description: Natural killer cells expressing NKG7 and granzymes, with cytotoxic function and CD16-mediated antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity.

Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cell (pDC).description: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells expressing CLEC4C (BDCA-2) and IL3RA (CD123), specialized in type I interferon production in response to viral infections.

CD4 CTL.description: CD4+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes that express both CD4 and a range of cytotoxic molecules such as granzymes and perforin.

CD8 CTL.description: CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes expressing CD8, granzymes, and perforin, specialized for killing infected cells.

NK cells.description: Natural killer cells expressing CD16 and CD56, with potent cytotoxic activity and without prior sensitization.

NKT cells.description: Invariant natural killer T cells that co-express T cell receptor and NK cell markers, recognizing lipid antigens via CD1d.

γδ T cells.description: Gamma-delta T cells expressing γδ T cell receptor, bridging innate and adaptive immunity with rapid cytotoxic responses.

Naive CD4+ T cell.description: Quiescent CD4+ T cells expressing CD45RA and CCR7, with high expression of IL7R and SELL, and lacking effector molecules.

Recent thymic emigrant (RTE) CD4+.description: Recent thymic emigrant subset of naive CD4+ T cells expressing CD31 (PECAM1) and high levels of PTK7.

CD8+ Naive T cell.description: Naive CD8+ T cells with high expression of CD8A, CD8B, and CCR7, SELL, and IL7R.

CD4+ Central Memory T cell.description: Central memory CD4+ T cells expressing CCR7 and CD45RO, with high ANXA1 and LGALS3.

CD4+ Effector Memory T cell.description: Effector memory CD4+ T cells lacking CCR7, expressing KLRG1 and cytolytic molecules like GZMA and IFNG.

CD4 Naive.description: CD4+ T cells that have not encountered antigen, characterized by high expression of SELL and CCR7, recirculating through lymph nodes.

CD4 Memory.description: Antigen-experienced CD4+ T cells that provide rapid recall responses, expressing IL7R and homing to lymph nodes and tissues.

CD4 Regulatory.description: Immunosuppressive CD4+ T cells that express FOXP3 and CD25, maintaining self-tolerance and controlling immune responses.

CD8 Proliferating.description: Proliferating CD8+ cytotoxic T cells undergoing cell division, marked by high expression of MKI67 and STMN1, often expanding during immune responses.

NK cells.description: Innate lymphoid cells that kill infected or transformed cells without prior sensitization, expressing NKG7 and cytotoxic granules.

CD4 TCM.description: CD4+ central memory T cells express lymph node homing markers (CCR7, SELL) and have memory function with high proliferative capacity.

CD4 Naive.description: Naive CD4+ T cells are antigen-inexperienced, express high levels of CD45RA and lymph node homing receptors, and have limited effector function.

CD4 TEM.description: CD4+ effector memory T cells are antigen-experienced, lack lymph node homing molecules, and produce effector cytokines such as IFN-γ and TNF.

Treg.description: Regulatory T cells suppress immune responses and express FOXP3, high levels of CD25, and inhibitory molecules like CTLA4.

CD8 TCM.description: CD8+ central memory T cells are antigen-experienced, express lymph node homing markers, and have memory function with proliferative potential.

CD4 TEM Th1.description: CD4+ effector memory T cells polarized toward Th1, characterized by expression of IFN-γ, TBX21, and CXCR3, involved in cell-mediated immunity.

CD4 TEM Th2.description: CD4+ effector memory T cells polarized toward Th2, characterized by expression of IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, GATA3, and CCR4, promoting humoral and allergic responses.

CD4 TEM Th17.description: CD4+ effector memory T cells polarized toward Th17, characterized by expression of IL-17A, RORC, CCR6, and IL-23R, involved in neutrophil recruitment and autoimmune inflammation.

CD4 TEM Treg.description: CD4+ effector memory regulatory T cells, characterized by FOXP3, CD25, and CTLA4 expression, suppressing immune responses and maintaining self-tolerance.

CD8 TEM.description: CD8+ effector memory T cells, cytotoxic lymphocytes expressing granzymes, perforin, and IFN-γ, targeting infected or malignant cells.

NK cells.description: Natural killer cells, innate lymphoid cells with cytolytic activity, expressing NKG7, perforin, and granzymes, involved in early defense against tumors and viruses.

CD8 Naive.description: Naive CD8+ T cells expressing CCR7 and CD45RA, responsible for lymph node homing and long-term persistence.

CD8 Memory.description: Memory CD8+ T cells with cytotoxic potential and expression of chemokine receptors, enabling rapid response to secondary infections.

CD4 Naive.description: Naive CD4+ T cells that circulate through lymph nodes and differentiate into helper T cell subsets upon activation.

NK cells.description: Natural killer cells that mediate innate cytotoxicity through secretion of perforin and granzymes, and express activating receptors.

CD8 Proliferating.description: Proliferating CD8+ T cells with high expression of cell cycle and proliferation markers (MKI67, TOP2A) along with CD8 and CD3 complex genes.

CD8 Effector Memory.description: CD8+ effector memory T cells expressing cytotoxic molecules (GZMK, GZMB, PRF1) and chemokines (CCL5) with a memory-associated phenotype.

CD8 Naive.description: Naive CD8+ T cells characterized by high expression of homing markers CCR7, SELL, and transcription factors TCF7, LEF1, with low cytotoxic molecule expression.

NK.description: Natural killer cells expressing cytotoxic granules (NKG7, GNLY, PRF1) and various killer cell lectin-like receptors, with high expression of FCGR3A (CD16).

CD4 Proliferating.description: Proliferating CD4+ T cells with high expression of cell cycle and proliferation markers (MKI67, TOP2A) along with CD4 and CD3 complex genes, often confused with CD8 Proliferating.

CD8 TCM.description: Central memory CD8+ T cells; express lymph node homing markers (CCR7, SELL) and retain proliferative capacity.

CD8 TEM.description: Effector memory CD8+ T cells; exhibit immediate cytotoxic functions and express granzymes and perforin.

CD8 Naive.description: Naive CD8+ T cells; antigen-inexperienced, express lymph node homing receptors and lack effector molecules.

CD4 TCM.description: Central memory CD4+ T cells; provide helper functions and express lymph node homing markers.

NK cells.description: Natural killer cells; innate lymphoid cells with cytotoxic activity against infected or transformed cells.

CD8 TEM.description: CD8 effector memory T cells characterized by rapid cytotoxic effector functions and expression of granzymes and perforin.

CD8 CM.description: CD8 central memory T cells characterized by lymph node homing and self-renewal capacity with expression of CCR7 and CD62L.

CD8 Naive.description: CD8 naive T cells that are antigen-inexperienced with high expression of lymph node homing markers and transcription factors TCF7 and LEF1.

CD8 TEMRA.description: CD8 terminally differentiated effector memory cells re-expressing CD45RA, with high expression of KLRG1, CD57, and potent cytotoxicity.

NK cells.description: Natural killer cells characterized by expression of NKG7, GNLY, and FCGR3A, with potent cytotoxic and cytokine-producing functions.

cDC1.description: Conventional type 1 dendritic cells, specialized in cross-presentation of antigens to CD8+ T cells.

cDC2.description: Conventional type 2 dendritic cells, efficient in MHC-II presentation and CD4+ T cell activation.

pDC.description: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells, specialized in producing type I interferons in response to viral infections.

CD14+ Monocyte.description: CD14+ classical monocytes, involved in phagocytosis and inflammatory responses.

cDC2.description: Conventional dendritic cells type 2, expressing CD1c and FcεRI, specialized in antigen presentation to CD4+ T cells.

CD14+ Monocytes.description: CD14+ classical monocytes, phagocytic cells that can differentiate into macrophages or dendritic cells and produce inflammatory cytokines.

cDC1.description: Conventional dendritic cells type 1, expressing CD141 (BDCA-3), specialized in cross-presentation and activation of CD8+ T cells.

pDC.description: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells, major producers of type I interferons in response to viral infection, expressing CD123 and CD303.

MAIT cells.description: Mucosal-associated invariant T cells, an innate-like T cell subset characterized by semi-invariant TCR and high expression of CD161, involved in antimicrobial immunity.

γδ T cells.description: Gamma-delta T cells, a subset of T cells expressing gamma-delta T cell receptor, with roles in innate and adaptive immunity.

NK cells.description: Natural killer cells, innate lymphoid cells that mediate cytotoxicity against infected or malignant cells without prior sensitization.

CD8+ T cells.description: Cytotoxic T lymphocytes expressing CD8, central to adaptive immune response against intracellular pathogens.

CD14+ Monocyte.description: Classical monocyte expressing CD14 and high levels of phagocytosis-related genes.

CD8+ T cell.description: Cytotoxic T lymphocyte with effector functions and granzyme production.

NK cell.description: Natural killer cell with innate cytotoxic activity and interferon-gamma production.

B cell.description: Antibody-producing B lymphocyte with MHC class II expression.

Plasmacytoid dendritic cell.description: Type I interferon-producing dendritic cell with plasmacytoid morphology.

Erythroid Progenitor.description: Early committed erythroid progenitor cells with high expression of erythroid transcription factors and transferrin receptor, precursor to mature erythroblasts.

Erythroblast.description: Mature erythroblasts with high hemoglobin synthesis and enucleation markers, representing the final stage of erythroid development.

Megakaryocyte.description: Megakaryocytic cells expressing platelet-specific markers and transcription factors regulating megakaryopoiesis, commonly confused with erythroid cells due to shared GATA1 expression.

Platelet.description: Platelet fragments expressing megakaryocytic and granule marker genes, often contaminating PBMC single-cell data and confused with erythroid cells.

Vδ2 T cells.description: Vδ2 T cells are the predominant gamma-delta T cell subset in human peripheral blood, characterized by expression of Vδ2 TCR chain and high cytotoxic activity against microbes and tumors.

Vδ1 T cells.description: Vδ1 T cells are a less abundant PBMC gamma-delta subset that often reside in tissues and exhibit regulatory and cytotoxic functions, with a naïve/memory phenotype.

CD8+ T cells.description: CD8+ T cells are cytotoxic T lymphocytes that recognize peptide antigens presented by MHC class I, playing a central role in adaptive immunity.

NK cells.description: Natural killer (NK) cells are innate lymphoid cells that kill infected or tumor cells without prior sensitization, characterized by expression of CD56 and CD16.

MAIT cells.description: Mucosal-associated invariant T (MAIT) cells are an innate-like T cell subset that recognizes microbial vitamin B metabolites presented by MR1, expressing CD161 and semi-invariant TCR.

HSC.description: Self-renewing hematopoietic stem cells giving rise to all blood lineages.

MPP.description: Multipotent progenitors with limited self-renewal and multilineage differentiation capacity.

CMP.description: Common myeloid progenitors committed to myeloid lineage (monocytes, granulocytes, erythrocytes, megakaryocytes).

Pre-B cell.description: Early B cell progenitor undergoing immunoglobulin gene rearrangement.

Monocyte.description: Circulating monocytes, innate immune phagocytes with pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory functions.

ILC1.description: Innate lymphoid cell type 1 involved in type 1 immunity, producing interferon-gamma and requiring T-bet.

ILC2.description: Innate lymphoid cell type 2 involved in type 2 immunity, producing IL-5 and IL-13, dependent on GATA3.

ILC3.description: Innate lymphoid cell type 3 involved in mucosal immunity, producing IL-22 and IL-17, dependent on RORγt.

NK cells.description: Natural killer cells, cytotoxic innate lymphocytes that kill infected or transformed cells, often confused with ILC1 due to shared markers.

MAIT.description: Mucosal-associated invariant T cells, a subset of innate-like T cells that express a semi-invariant TCR (TRAV1-2/TRAJ33) and recognize bacterial metabolites, characterized by high expression of KLRB1, IL18R1, and SLC4A10.

CD8+ T cell.description: Conventional cytotoxic CD8+ T cells that mediate adaptive immunity, characterized by expression of CD8A, CD8B, and effector molecules such as GZMB and PRF1.

NKT cell.description: Invariant natural killer T cells that recognize glycolipid antigens presented by CD1d, defined by expression of ZBTB16, TRAV10, and TRAJ18, and share some markers with MAIT cells.

Gamma-delta T cell.description: T cells expressing gamma-delta TCR (TRDC, TRGC1/2) that function in innate immunity, often found in tissues, and can be confused with MAIT cells due to overlapping cytotoxicity markers.

CD56bright NK.description: CD56bright NK cells are cytokine-producing, immunoregulatory NK cells with high expression of CD56, NKG2A, and CD94, and low cytotoxicity.

CD56dim NK.description: CD56dim NK cells are highly cytotoxic, CD16-positive NK cells that mediate antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and express killer immunoglobulin-like receptors.

NKT cell.description: NKT cells are a subset of T cells that co-express NK cell markers and a semi-invariant T-cell receptor, recognizing lipid antigens presented by CD1d.

CD8+ TEMRA.description: CD8+ TEMRA cells are terminally differentiated effector memory T cells re-expressing CD45RA, with high cytotoxic potential and expression of NK-like receptors.

NK CD56bright.description: CD56bright NK cells are abundant in lymph nodes and produce abundant cytokines such as IFN-gamma and TNF-alpha, with lower cytotoxicity.

NK CD56dim.description: CD56dim NK cells are highly cytotoxic and constitute the majority of circulating NK cells, expressing high levels of CD16 and perforin.

NK Proliferating.description: Proliferating NK cells are actively cycling, expressing high levels of cell cycle-related genes such as MKI67 and TOP2A, and are typically a small subset in PBMC.

CD8+ T cells (activated).description: Activated CD8+ T cells are cytotoxic T lymphocytes that proliferate and produce effector molecules, often confused with NK cells due to shared markers like GZMB and PRF1.

NKT cells.description: NKT cells are a subset of T cells that express both T cell receptors and NK cell markers, capable of rapid cytokine production and often misidentified as NK cells.

NK_CD56bright.description: Cytokine-producing NK cells characterized by high CD56 expression, low CD16, and expressing KIT and IL7R, with a regulatory/immature phenotype.

NK_CD56dim.description: Cytotoxic NK cells with high CD16 expression, low CD56, and expressing granzymes and perforin, constituting the majority of peripheral blood NK cells.

CD8_T_cell.description: Cytotoxic T lymphocytes expressing CD8 and CD3, with T cell receptor complex genes, involved in adaptive immune response.

NKT_cell.description: Innate-like T lymphocytes that express both T cell and NK cell markers, notably KLRB1 and ZBTB16, and recognize lipid antigens via CD1d.

pDC_resting.description: Resting plasmacytoid dendritic cells with high expression of CLEC4C and IL3RA, involved in antiviral IFN production.

pDC_activated.description: Activated plasmacytoid dendritic cells with high expression of GZMB and IRF7, producing type I interferons upon viral stimulation.

cDC2.description: Conventional dendritic cells type 2, highly expressing CD1c and FCER1A, specialized in antigen presentation to CD4+ T cells.

CD14+ monocyte.description: Classical monocytes expressing CD14 and FcγRIIIa, key in innate immunity and often confused with pDCs in flow cytometry.

Plasmablast.description: Plasmablasts are proliferating antibody-secreting B cell precursors that highly express PRDM1, XBP1, IRF4, and MKI67, along with cell cycle genes and immunoglobulin chains.

Plasma cell.description: Plasma cells are terminally differentiated antibody-secreting cells with high SDC1, PRDM1, XBP1, and immunoglobulin heavy chains, and they lack proliferation markers like MKI67.

Memory B cell.description: Memory B cells are long-lived B cells expressing CD27, CD19, MS4A1, and class-switched or unswitched immunoglobulins, along with activation markers and transcription factors like BCL6.

Naive B cell.description: Naive B cells are resting B cells expressing surface IgM and IgD, along with CD19, MS4A1, PAX5, and TCL1A, but lacking CD27 and CD38.

Resting Platelet.description: Inactive platelets circulating in blood, expressing alpha-granule proteins and surface receptors.

Activated Platelet.description: Platelets that have undergone degranulation and shape change, expressing activation markers like P-selectin and CD63.

Megakaryocyte.description: Bone marrow precursor of platelets, occasionally found in PBMC, expressing high levels of platelet-specific genes and cell cycle markers.

Erythrocyte.description: Red blood cells, enucleated cells expressing hemoglobin genes and membrane proteins, often contaminating PBMC preparations.

Naive Treg.description: Naive Treg cells are a subset of regulatory T cells with a CD45RA+FOXP3lo phenotype, expressing high levels of CCR7 and CD62L for lymphoid homing and low levels of activation markers.

Effector Treg.description: Effector Treg cells are highly suppressive regulatory T cells with a CD45RA-FOXP3hi phenotype, expressing elevated levels of activation markers, costimulatory molecules, and effector cytokines such as IL-10 and TGF-beta.

CD4+ Conv T.description: Conventional CD4+ T cells are a heterogeneous population of helper T cells that do not express FOXP3 at high levels and include Th1, Th2, Th17, and Tfh subsets with diverse cytokine profiles.

CD8+ T.description: CD8+ T cells are cytotoxic T lymphocytes that are primarily responsible for killing infected or malignant cells, expressing CD8 and containing perforin and granzymes.

Th17.description: Th17 cells are a subset of CD4+ T cells characterized by expression of RORC and production of IL-17A and IL-17F, playing a key role in mucosal immunity and autoimmune inflammation.
